summary:
The United States has proposed tariffs of up to 20% on 14 economies, including China and the EU, a week after Xi Jinping met Donald Trump in Shenzhen. The measures aim to counter excessive manufacturing abroad. By another count, the proposal covers 16 trading partners, including China.

Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's financial district and the Ras Tanura refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. A fire was reported at Ras Tanura, and the financial district was attacked for the second time in a week.

Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a security pact seen as countering China, making Australia the archipelago's primary security partner. The Solomon Islands must consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals, and the accord precludes such bases. A 2022 agreement with China had raised concerns that Beijing could establish a military presence on the island.

headlines.title: Solomon Islands signs security pact with Australia

headlines.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills Hamas security chief and family
headlines.summary: An Israeli air strike on a Gaza apartment killed Naeem Abu Nahel, a Hamas internal security chief who had held the post for two months, along with his wife and daughters. The Israeli military said it 'targeted a Hamas terrorist', and seven Palestinians were reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.

headlines.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 with first Pakistani astronaut
headlines.summary: China launched the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft on Wednesday with two Chinese astronauts and a Pakistani, the first foreign crew member sent to its Tiangong space station. The spacecraft separated from its rocket and entered its predetermined orbit.

headlines.title: Bangladesh raises garment workers' minimum wage by 36%
headlines.summary: Bangladesh raised the minimum monthly wage for garment workers by 36% to 17,000 taka, about $138, officials said on Wednesday. The increase followed weeks of sometimes violent protests that caused hundreds of millions of dollars in business losses.

headlines.title: Colombian forces rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
headlines.summary: Security forces rescued all hostages held at a supermarket in Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday, after a siege lasting nearly a day, or 17 hours by another count. One gunman was killed in the operation to free around 20 shoppers and employees.
